A1.justification: The PDFs clearly describe the same work despite the title and method-name changes. All supplied pages, equations, figures and tables are readable. Neither PDF contains an appendix or embedded supplement; separately mentioned supplementary material is unavailable and is not treated as inspected evidence.

before.justification: v1 reports original super-resolution benchmark results, inference measurements, and training-data, perceptual-loss and discriminator ablations in Section 4 and Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results for D3SR, public-data training variants, inference measurements and ablations in Section 4, Tables 1–6 and Figure 3.

M1.justification: The one-step generator, noisy-latent discriminator, LoRA training and MSE plus EA-DISTS/adversarial objectives remain. SDXL discrimination was already proposed and tested in v1 Section 3.4 and Table 6; promoting it to the main configuration does not introduce a new procedure. Renaming DFOSD to D3SR and describing it as distillation do not establish an algorithmic change.

E1.justification: v3 replaces DRealSR evaluation with synthetically degraded DIV2K-val, changing coverage from three real-world datasets to two real-world datasets plus a synthetic test scenario. RealSR and RealSet65 remain. LSDIR plus FFHQ training is not new coverage: v1 already used it in the training-data ablation.

E2.justification: v3 adds evaluated AddSR one-step and four-step comparisons. Real-ESRGAN and SwinIR disappear from quantitative full-reference comparisons, while ResShift and SinSR disappear from the complexity table. Discriminator controls are also substantively redescribed. LDL and FeMASR are newly listed, but the supplied v3 contains no corresponding results establishing their evaluated participation.

E3.justification: The main discriminator changes from SD 2.1-base to the previously tested SDXL configuration, and reported batch size changes from 16 to 8. v3 drops ClipIQA, adds LPIPS to ablation reporting, and specifies Real-ESRGAN degradation for synthetic DIV2K-val evaluation. Its discriminator controls are described differently from v1's SD-initialized controls; this establishes revised reported settings, not that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The central discriminator ablation is recast from comparing SD-initialized discriminator designs to interpreting pretrained versus randomly initialized discrimination, with a pixel-space CNN control. Figure 3 extends scaling analysis to SD 1.5. Public-versus-collected training comparisons expand across benchmarks, while v1's dedicated training-data and PSNR/SSIM visual case studies are absent from supplied v3. The perceptual-loss variants remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Neither establishes a statistical uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark and ablation results are substantially replaced or extended. For example, main RealSR NIQE changes from 3.9255 to 3.747, while PSNR changes from 24.60 to 23.98; these accompany changed training settings and are not same-setting gains or losses. v3 adds DIV2K-val, AddSR and broader public-training results, and removes DRealSR and ClipIQA entries. The proposed model's reported 0.11-second inference time remains unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes the redundant expression following Equation 3 that defined the predicted latent using total timestep T, conflicting with Equation 1's intermediate timestep T_L. This eliminates a local mathematical inconsistency. The numbered diffusion, adversarial-loss, Sobel and EA-DISTS equations otherwise retain their substance; no new proofs or theoretical guarantees appear.

C1.justification: The main contribution changes from explicitly distillation-free training with a noise-aware discriminator to a diffusion-distillation approach centered on a large discriminator. Reduced training overhead loses its former prominence. v3 also introduces broad headline claims of at least threefold faster inference and at least 30% fewer parameters, while retaining the EA-DISTS and perceptual-quality claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explanation linking VSD's reliance on pretrained priors and distribution mismatch to unrealistic textures, and interprets the discriminator comparison as evidence for pretraining. It removes v1 Section 5's specific training-memory and latency arguments against SinSR and OSEDiff. The broader interpretations concerning teacher limitations, discriminator scaling and perceptual versus full-reference quality largely persist.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the first 10,000 FFHQ images and a 95,000-image public training collection. It no longer explicitly describes learning the text embedding during training, instead mentioning fixed conditioning at inference. The repository pointer changes from DFOSD to D3SR, but both versions only promise code and model release. The newly mentioned supplementary pseudocode and hyperparameter values are not present in the supplied PDF.

R1.justification: v3 adds substantive positioning against Diffusion-GAN, DDGAN, ADD and LADD in Section 3.2, and expands one-step super-resolution coverage to YONOS-SR, AddSR, TAD-SR and TSD-SR. This accompanies a significant repositioning from avoiding distillation to performing adversarial diffusion distillation, beyond bibliographic or citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, introduction and discriminator explanation are substantially rewritten around D3SR and large-discriminator distillation. Terminology changes throughout, the separate comparison discussion in v1 Section 5 disappears, and metric explanations and the conclusion are condensed. These are substantial narrative changes beyond adding experimental content.

P2.justification: v3 changes to a two-column layout, redraws the training diagram, and reorganizes benchmark tables with methods as rows and combined reference/no-reference metrics. It adds the discriminator-scaling chart, removes several dedicated visual comparisons, and reduces the main qualitative montage from four examples to three. Retained feature and loss visualizations are relocated or rearranged.

improvement.justification: AddSR comparisons, synthetic evaluation, broader public-training results and stronger related-work positioning improve the evidence and context. However, the new broad efficiency claims exceed the narrowed comparison: v1 Table 3 reports SinSR at 0.16 seconds versus 0.11 seconds for the proposed method, far short of threefold, and v3 omits SinSR from its efficiency table. Revised discriminator-control descriptions also retain earlier control scores without explaining the discrepancy. These benefits and evidential weaknesses leave the net quality change uncertain.
